title: Clarify drag and drop pointer events
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? Pointer events seem different for every combination of pointer input and browser, so before filing bugs, I would like to know what is considered ok behavior. First, I have two questions: Why would the source node match `:active` and `:hover`, and what is the purpose of that? When the [Pointer Event spec says](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#suppressing-a-pointer-event-stream): >

The user agent MUST run the following steps to suppress a pointer event stream:

>
    >
  • Fire a pointercancel event.
    • >
  • Fire a pointerout event.
    • >
  • Fire a pointerleave event.
    • >
  • Implicitly release the pointer capture if the pointer is currently captured.
    • >
Is it fine even if pointerout and pointerleave aren't fired immediately, but after a while?
Not knowing much, I would have expected something like this ``` pointerdown
section:active:hover div:active:hover pointermove
section:active:hover div:active:hover dragstart
section:active:hover div:active:hover pointercancel
pointerout
pointerleave
pointerleave
dragenter
... dragleave
dragend
```
--- Test [drag.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22806140/drag.html) page: https://codepen.io/sb3nder/full/GgoEoLW Structure: ```html
drag me
``` Step to reproduce: drag div outside section. --- ## Chrome
mouse drag ``` pointerdown

section:active:hover div:active:hover dragstart

section:active:hover div:active:hover dragenter
section:active:hover div:active:hover ... dragleave
section:active:hover div:active:hover dragend

pointerleave
```

Source node doesn't match `:hover`. ---
touch drag (hold) ``` pointerdown

section:active:hover div:active:hover pointerleave
section:active:hover div:active:hover dragend
```
`pointercancel` is fired after the DND operation, instead of before, as the [living spec states](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#drag-and-drop-processing-model): >10.

Fire a pointer event at the source node named pointercancel, and fire any other follow-up events as required by Pointer Events. [POINTEREVENTS]

I don't think `dragend` timing is right. ---
pen drag (hold) ``` pointerdown

`pointercancel` is not fired as the living spec states. `pointerout` and `pointerleave` are fired a second time. --- ## Firefox
